name: Royal Gold, Inc

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, filed 2026-02-19, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (in thousands): the investing-activities section lists ONLY Sandstorm & Horizon acquisition, net of cash acquired $(411,342) for 2025 (none in 2024/2023), Acquisition of stream and royalty interests $(1,164,753) / $(102,564) / $(2,678) for 2025/2024/2023, Proceeds from the sale of the Versamet Shares and other securities $158,886 (2025 only), Cash calls for Hod Maden equity method investment $(9,330) (2025 only), Proceeds from Khoemacau debt facility $25,000 (2024 only), Proceeds from the sale of inventory - restricted $7,681 (2025 only), and Other $299 / $(116) / $(151) — net cash used in investing activities $(1,418,559) / $(77,680) / $(2,829). There is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment line anywhere in the statement for any of the three years, and the balance sheet carries no property and equipment asset line (the engine's financials_history.csv ppe_net is blank for every year).
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 in EDGAR companyfacts under every candidate tag the engine reads, because Royal Gold buys no property or equipment: it is a royalty/stream company whose investing outflows are acquisitions of stream and royalty interests (a separate, growth-investment line the standardized PPE-capex definition does not deduct — the company's own free-cash-flow definition, OCF minus acquisition of stream and royalty interests, is discussed in analysis.md). The filing's cash-flow statement fully accounts for investing activities for all three years with no PPE purchase line, so PPE capex is $0 as a filing fact, not an estimate. Measured impact is nil: the engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure — it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.
